evidence.basis_note: This figure is Capability Coverage C, computed on the fixed 88-point denominator per capability_universe.json capability_coverage.formula. It is independent of the common-basis vs all-fragments distinction used for metrics A-D/E.
evidence.formula: C = 100 * (sum over 44 probes of capability_points * support_factor) / 88
evidence.limitations: This is a single-worker desk assessment against the frozen rubric text and documented Kotlin/JVM language behavior; it was not produced by an automated build/run harness inside this packet-only environment. Every support level cites the specific language rule or stdlib fact relied upon, per adjudication_and_audit.evidence_required_per_pair, for downstream mechanical/human audit.
evidence.na_policy_note: No probe was excluded or marked N/A for Kotlin. All 4 NONE results (F04.P1, F05.P2, F20.P1, F20.P2) retain their full capability_points in the denominator per NA-2/NA-6; each carries a written N-1 citation.

F01.P1.note: val n = 7; return n. val is Kotlin's non-reassignable local binding form.

F01.P2.note: top-level var counter: Long = 0 (mutable); const val LIMIT: Long = 100 (compile-time constant, primitive type allowed for const val).

F02.P1.note: Kotlin performs definite-assignment analysis: `val v: Int` (or var) declared without initializer, assigned on both branches of an if/else, then read is accepted by the compiler.

F02.P2.note: Kotlin stdlib has no documented mechanism for genuinely uninitialized bulk storage; ByteArray(16) always zero-fills. Substituted the zero-initialized ByteArray per R9 named-substitution exception for F02.P2. Never FULL per rubric.

F03.P2.note: xs[1] = 42 on a MutableList, in-place element mutation via operator convention (set).

F04.P1.citation: Kotlin has no reference/pointer/inout type for a local scalar (Int) variable; two names cannot denote the same primitive storage with write access through both without wrapping in an object/array, which the probe does not permit as FULL substitute. No documented standard mechanism exists.

F04.P2.note: kotlin.collections.List is a read-only view interface; `val window: List<Int> = xs` upcasts the existing MutableList reference without copying elements (Kotlin stdlib docs: List does not guarantee immutability of the underlying collection, only that this reference cannot mutate it).

F04.P3.note: class Handle(val id: Int); val first = Handle(5); val box = mutableListOf(first); val second = box[0]; val same = (first === second) — Kotlin's `===` is the standard referential-identity operator, distinct from `==` (structural equality).

F05.P1.note: f(x) — Kotlin's ordinary call syntax has no sigils; JVM reference-passing semantics for a MutableList argument, so the callee's access is not determinable at the call site alone.

F05.P2.citation: Kotlin has no `inout`/`ref`/pointer parameter-passing form for a scalar Int; the only route is a mutable wrapper object/array, which support_rubric.P-a explicitly disallows as a FULL substitute for this probe (wrapping the integer in a mutable container/object is NOT an acceptable substitute for FULL) and F05.P2 is on the N-4 no-fragment list.

F05.P3.note: val neg: (Int) -> Int = { a -> k - a } (captures k by closure); val ys = xs.map(neg) — neg passed by name at the map argument position.

F06.P1.note: fun mid(xs: List<Int>): Int = xs[1]; val y = mid(xs); return y.

F06.P2.note: fun divmod2(a: Int, b: Int): Pair<Int,Int> = Pair(a/b, a%b); val (q, r) = divmod2(a,b); return q+r — Kotlin Pair plus destructuring binding.

F07.P1.note: val r = a * b + c, ordinary operator precedence.

F07.P2.note: val q = a / b (Int division, truncates toward zero); val m = a % b (remainder follows dividend sign); val d = a.toDouble() / b — explicit conversion required for real division since Kotlin has no implicit numeric widening.

F08.P1.note: val m = Int.MAX_VALUE; val o = m + 1 — Kotlin/JVM Int arithmetic wraps silently on overflow (two's-complement, documented JVM/Kotlin numeric behavior); no standard checked/saturating stdlib op exists, so rung (iv) plain operator is used and its outcome is determinate from documentation.

F08.P2.note: val q = if (b == 0) 0 else a / b — explicit local guard (rung ii); Kotlin stdlib provides no checked-division-to-optional operation.

F09.P1.note: val eq = (s1 == s2) — Kotlin's == calls equals() (structural/content comparison) by language definition, distinct from === (identity).

F09.P2.note: xs.sortedWith(compareByDescending { it }) (explicit descending ordering value, returns new List) and val lt = a < b.

F10.P1.note: val small = big.toInt() — explicit ordinary narrowing conversion (rung ii); Kotlin stdlib has no checked Long-to-Int conversion returning an optional, so the plain explicit conversion (bit-truncating) is used.

F10.P2.note: val sum = i.toDouble() + d — Kotlin requires an explicit conversion call since it performs no implicit numeric widening between Int and Double.

F11.P1.note: val e = xs[i]; return e — throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range index (documented, unchecked at compile time). getOrNull(i) recorded separately as the .checked evidence-only variant.

F11.P2.note: val part = xs.subList(1, 4) — List.subList is documented to return a view backed by the original list; element production via part[0].

F12.P1.note: val o: Int? = null; val n = o ?: 0 — Kotlin nullable type plus elvis operator standard fallback form.

F12.P2.note: val h: (Int) -> Int = { a -> a + 1 }; val p: Int? = o?.let(h); val result = p ?: 0 — safe-call plus let, no explicit if/when.

F13.P1.note: fun parseTwice(s: String): Int { val n = s.toInt(); return n * 2 } — toInt() throws NumberFormatException on failure and propagates unhandled (Kotlin/JVM has no checked exceptions, so this is the normal propagation mechanism).

F13.P2.note: val n = try { s.toInt() } catch (e: NumberFormatException) { 0 }; return n.

F14.P1.note: sealed class Shape; data class Circle(val r: Double): Shape(); data class Rect(val w: Double, val h: Double): Shape() — Kotlin sealed classes are compiler-enforced closed to the same module (cannot be subclassed from outside).

F14.P2.note: val area = when (s) { is Circle -> PI*s.r*s.r; is Rect -> s.w*s.h } — when-as-expression over a sealed class is exhaustiveness-checked by the compiler with no else arm required.

F14.P3.note: interface Shape { fun area(): Double } with Circle/Rect implementations in `shapes` unit; a separate unit defines class Tri: Shape and dispatches through a Shape-typed value — ordinary open interface implementation across compilation units, using the multi_unit_recipe (kotlinc util.kt FILE.kt ...).

F15.P1.note: fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T = xs[0] — parametric function reused at Int and String element types with T recoverable statically at each call site.

F15.P2.note: fun <T : Comparable<T>> maxOf2(a: T, b: T): T = if (a > b) a else b — declaration-site bound (Comparable<T>) checked at the generic's own declaration.

F15.P3.note: interface Named { fun tag(): String }; class A: Named; class B: Named; val items: List<Named> = listOf(A(), B()); items[0].tag() dispatches at runtime through the abstract element type.

F16.P1.note: val xs = mutableListOf(1,2,3); val total = xs.sum() — standard stdlib reduction.

F16.P2.note: val mp = mapOf("a" to 1); val total = mp.values.sum(); val miss = mp["b"] ?: 0 — mapOf documented to preserve insertion iteration order (LinkedHashMap-backed); missing-key lookup via [] returns null, handled by elvis default.

F17.P1.note: File("data.txt").bufferedReader().use { it.readText() } — Closeable.use is Kotlin stdlib's scoped-cleanup mechanism, guarantees close() on every exit path including exceptions, analogous to try-with-resources.

F17.P2.note: Kotlin/JVM has no deterministic end-of-lifetime hook (finalize() is deprecated/nondeterministic); substituted an explicit close()/dispose invoked by the `use{}` scoped construct incrementing `released`, per the probe's own named substitution clause (F17.P2 is in the R9 exception list). Never FULL.

F18.P1.note: println("x") — kotlin.io is implicitly available with no import required, satisfying 'nothing if the facility is available without one'.

F18.P2.note: util.kt: `fun pubAdd(a: Int, b: Int) = a + b + secret()` (public/exported by default) and `private fun secret() = 1` (Kotlin top-level `private` restricts visibility to the declaring file); external call `util.pubAdd(2,3)` via package-qualified import, using the frozen multi_unit_recipe.

F19.P1.note: Two java.util.concurrent.Executors-submitted tasks (Future<Int>) computing 20 and 22, joined via future.get() on both, summed to 42 — java.util.concurrent ships as part of the JVM/JDK that the frozen `kotlinc`/`java` recipe already depends on, with no separate package fetch (kotlinx.coroutines was excluded as a non-bundled third-party artifact).

F19.P2.note: java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong counter, incremented 1000 times from two threads via counter.incrementAndGet() (JDK-documented atomic read-modify-write), joined, final value 2000; verified deterministic per the atomic contract.

F20.P1.citation: Kotlin's frozen JVM recipe (kotlinc -include-runtime / java -jar) has no built-in, standard-library FFI mechanism to declare and call a native C function (JNI requires hand-written native glue and a separate native build step outside the frozen recipe; the JDK Foreign Function & Memory API is not a stable, universally-shipped stdlib feature across the frozen toolchain).

F20.P2.citation: Kotlin's frozen recipe compiles to a JVM .jar, not a native compiled artifact; there is no unmangled, nm-checkable C-ABI symbol to export. Per rubric N-3 clause for F20.P2, this is recorded as NONE with the `nm` field reading 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'.
